candidates.title: Weekly AI agent run summary

demandEvidence.chore: Summarize each agent's runs weekly for a team lead.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Schedule Trigger (weekly): summarize runs per agent for the team lead.

ease.reason: A student could test a weekly report on operator-supplied sample run rows; the assigned discussion gives no implementation reference.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a professional services team lead may value a recurring run summary; this post does not establish a buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can group supplied rows by agent and summarize them weekly, but no attached source documents a working automation capability.

autonomy.reason: A proposed scheduled report could summarize supplied rows; a person must provide reliable logs and check omissions, and implementation is unverified.

evidence.reason: The post specifies a weekly per-agent summary for a team lead, but gives no frequency history, data fields, or implementation proof.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore assessed with a mock weekly report, but no supplied building reference supports the automation. Excluded because it duplicates the other assigned agent-run logging chore and overlaps the recent AI-agent monitoring idea; it was also previously assessed without new evidence.

candidates.title: Log agent task outcomes to a sheet

demandEvidence.chore: Record each agent's name, task ID, status, and time in a Google Sheet when a task finishes or fails.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Every time an agent finishes or fails a task, Make should record the agent name, task ID, status and time in a Google Sheet.

ease.reason: A student can mock the four named fields in a sheet, but no attached building source documents a working Make integration.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a professional services team overseeing agents may value run records; the request establishes neither a paying customer nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype can accept simulated completion events and write the stated fields to a test sheet; live agent access is unsupported.

autonomy.reason: A proposed event-to-row loop is repeatable, but the source does not show integration mechanics and a person must verify missing or incorrect records.

evidence.reason: The request names the event and four output fields, but does not establish repeated demand beyond this post or implementation support.

candidates.reason: Concrete chore assessed as a simulated event-to-row experiment. Excluded as the same agent-run monitoring workflow and professional services customer as the assigned weekly summary, with no supplied building reference; this exact idea was previously excluded and no new evidence changes that decision.

candidates.title: Send a triggered email through Make

demandEvidence.chore: Send an email through an SMTP provider when another app triggers the scenario.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want a Make scenario to send an email through DigitalAka when a trigger occurs in another app.

ease.reason: A student can model the trigger and message with synthetic inputs, but no attached reference documents SMTP setup or delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a small professional services operator might value setup help, but this single integration question establishes no service buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A mock trigger-to-message plan is bounded, but provider configuration and real delivery cannot be verified with the supplied evidence.

autonomy.reason: A trigger could initiate a message in a proposed design, while a person must configure credentials and verify delivery; no reference supports these steps.

evidence.reason: The post clearly states the desired trigger and SMTP email task, but offers no repeated-work evidence or implementation proof.

candidates.reason: The trigger-to-email chore is concrete, but no supplied implementation reference supports a useful AI service or the provider setup. A mock is possible; a defensible supported experiment is not established, so it is excluded.

rejected.title: Ask whether Wikipedia may go away
rejected.reason: The post wonders whether Wikipedia is going away after an app advertisement appeared. It states no manual business chore, service request, or bounded automation task.

rejected.title: Inca 3D app launch
rejected.reason: The assigned excerpt is a product launch description, not a concrete customer chore or request for a service. No demand-backed experiment can be derived from this excerpt.

rejected.title: Learn an n8n project beyond a spreadsheet
rejected.reason: The author says they wanted a project beyond a form-to-spreadsheet exercise, but the assigned excerpt identifies no existing paying-customer task or requested service. Do not invent a duty from the expense-tracker title.

rejected.title: Assess caravan living during a rental crisis
rejected.reason: The post asks for opinions on caravan living as a housing stopgap. It does not request a concrete business task or automation service, and advice about housing suitability is not a supported narrow experiment.

rejected.title: Get beginner guidance for workflow automation
rejected.reason: The excerpt only says the poster is new to Make and wants guidance; it names no specific chore, output, or business service to automate.

steps.message: Assessed all eight assigned identities. Three concrete chores received provisional five-criterion assessments; none supports a distinct, sufficiently evidenced proposal. Five assignments lacked a concrete service chore. No post proposed.
